name: Dependency Injection Vocabulary
description: Controlled vocabulary for the Dependency Injection design pattern.

terms.definition: A pattern where an external assembler supplies a component's collaborators rather than the component creating them itself.
The principle that a framework controls program flow and component wiring, of which DI is one expression.
An object, service, or value that a component requires in order to do its work.
A dependency invoked by a component to fulfill part of its responsibility.
Injection style that supplies dependencies through the constructor.
Injection style that supplies dependencies through setter methods after construction.
Injection style in which the dependent implements an interface that the container calls to provide the dependency.
Injection style that passes dependencies as parameters to specific methods.
The single location, near program entry, where the object graph is assembled.
Framework component that resolves and wires dependencies based on registrations.
Alternative pattern in which components actively request dependencies from a registry.
Policy describing how long a resolved instance lives (singleton, scoped, transient).
Mapping from a service abstraction to its implementation and lifetime within a container.
Process of obtaining an instance of a registered service, recursively resolving its own dependencies.
Wrapping component registered with the container to add behavior around an existing service.
Component that participates in the resolution pipeline to apply cross-cutting concerns.
